subject: Dedicated capacity sizing follow-up / deployment mode clarification
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>

Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Quick recap + sizing questions (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private)

Hi Samir —

Thanks again for taking time today — really helpful to hear about FinLedger's planned LLM rollout. Quick recap and a few follow-ups so we can scope Dedicated capacity vs Hosted or Private options: 

Key points I noted from the call:
- Primary use: document parsing + abstractive summarization for financial reports (latency-sensitive on interactive flows).
- Expected launch: Q3 pilot (internal users), Q4 external beta.
- Data: mix of public & sensitive customer PII (we discussed VPC/private options).
- Goal: stable per-token cost and predictable latency for interactive product.

Sizing / qualification questions (short — answers will point us to Hosted API, Dedicated, or Private):
1) Preferred deployment mode? (Hosted API for speed, Dedicated reserved pool for predictable throughput, Private VPC/on-prem for strict data residency)
2) Target sustained TPS (inferences per second) and expected peak TPS/spike factor?
3) Concurrency (simultaneous requests)? Any batching on your side?
4) Typical token mix: average prompt length + average generated tokens; any long-context use (2k+ tokens)?
5) Any requirement for specific GPU types (A100 vs H100) or quantization restrictions?
6) SLA / uptime / compliance requirements (SOC2, audit log needs, retention)?

We're copying Aditya (solutions engineer) to start a lightweight sizing worksheet and propose options once we have the numbers. Attached is a blank workbook we'll populate together.

Next steps: if you can reply with the bullets above, Aditya and I will run throughput estimates and propose Dedicated pool sizing (GPU type, number of GPUs, baseline concurrency, and burst plan).

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Samir Gupta <samir@finledger.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 27 Feb 2026 10:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Quick recap + sizing questions (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private)

Marissa —

Appreciate the recap. Answers below (we kept the team loop small for this thread).

1) Deployment: we lean towards Dedicated capacity (reserved pool) to keep latency predictable and maintain an internal SLA for our customers. Private VPC is on the table for later (regulatory reasons) but not required for the pilot. Hosted API is attractive for PoC, but we need predictable throughput for the beta.

2) Throughput: target sustained ~50 TPS for inference requests during business hours. Peak spikes up to ~200 TPS for short windows (spike factor ~4).

3) Concurrency: typical concurrency ~10-20 concurrent requests; worst-case 40. We do some client-side batching (combine a few smaller items into a single request) but most requests are single-call interactive flows.

4) Token mix: average input prompt ~300 tokens, average generation ~500 tokens. Distribution roughly: 70% short prompts (~200–400 tokens total), 25% medium (~800–1200), 5% long (1.5–2k). For the pilot we expect average end-to-end tokens per request ~800.

5) GPU: H100 preferred for long-context and throughput but we are open to A100 if cost is significantly better. Quantization: we don't need anything exotic for the pilot — FP16/AMP or standard INT8 profiles are fine.

6) Compliance: SOC2 is required; data retention 90 days for logs, with PII redaction downstream. Audit logs and ability to integrate with our SIEM would be nice.

Let me know if you need exact qps traces or a sample request log. Happy to set a follow-up sizing call next week.

—Samir
Samir Gupta, Head of AI Platforms
FinLedger Inc.

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 28 Feb 2026 14:37:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Quick recap + sizing questions (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private)

Samir — thanks for the detailed answers, that's perfect. A couple of quick clarifications from the infra side so we size correctly: 

- When you say 50 TPS sustained with 200 TPS spikes, is that measured at the request level (i.e., each inference call counts as one TPS) or token TPS? We'll assume request-level TPS unless you confirm otherwise.
- For the concurrency numbers, are the worst-case 40 concurrent requests expected to be the long-tail (2k tokens) or short requests? Latency constraints depend heavily on request size distribution.
- Any expectation around tail latency (p95/p99) — e.g., p95 < 300ms for short prompts?

Prelim sizing notes based on your inputs (we'll refine after the call):
- Dedicated recommendation: H100-backed pool for best throughput on mixed workloads, or an A100-heavy pool with autoscaled H100 for long-context workloads to control cost.
- Starting pool suggestion: 4 x H100 (or 6 x A100) with continuous batching and prefix caching. This should cover ~50 sustained TPS with room for spikes using burst capacity (we'll detail burst policies).
- Concurrency handling: configure per-worker concurrency limit ~8 and use a fronting routing layer to spread requests across the pool.

I'll attach a populated sizing workbook and a simple network diagram showing VPC peering options for Dedicated and Private. Can we do a 30-min sizing call Monday 03/01 at 10:00 AM PST to finalize numbers and capture sample traces?

Thanks —
Aditya Rao
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
